extracted.intended_audience: funders, program staff, grantee organizations, and local news leaders evaluating newsroom sustainability
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluate the effects of philanthropic/grantee interventions on local newsroom sustainability using quantitative (audience, revenue, operations, staff) and qualitative (DEI, organizational practices, culture) measures, comparing pre- and post-intervention outcomes over short and multi-year horizons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Knight defines sustainability as “a newsroom where revenue outstrips expenses in a repeatable fashion, when sources of revenue are diversified, and audience size is consistent or growing year over year.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition is the anchor for the assessment. Measurement leverages both financial health and audience metrics, and the assessment also includes qualitative considerations (DEI, organizational practices, community representation) as part of sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial health (operating expenses-to-revenue ratio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether revenue outstrips expenses using the ratio of operating expenses divided by revenue; a ratio lower than 1 means an organization is cash flow positive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate the operating-expenses-to-revenue ratio from newsroom-reported figures and compare pre- and post-intervention and over time. Examples: AJP, INN and NRH SPS newsrooms showed revenue greater than expenditures in available data. Report sample sizes (n) and note exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revenue diversification
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsrooms should have diversified sources of revenue and reduced reliance on a single primary revenue source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track changes in the number and balance of revenue streams (e.g., earned revenue, individual donations, foundation/philanthropic funding, major gifts). Examples include newsrooms moving from one to two or two to three revenue sources; highlight whether charitable revenue increases are concentrated or broad-based.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience size and trend (DAMU)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure audience consistency or growth using digital average monthly users (DAMU) and compare changes year over year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use DAMU as a primary audience metric, comparing baseline to follow-up years and reporting averages/medians and n. Account for industry-wide trends (peak in 2020, general declines thereafter) and baseline effects (large-audience newsrooms can drive average declines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative indicators collected (audience, revenue, operations, staff)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect comparable quantitative data from newsrooms pre- and post-intervention and over longer terms (2–3 years) on audience, revenue, operations and staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardize metrics and baselines (e.g., 2019/2020 baselines) to enable longitudinal comparisons. Report completeness and sample sizes for each metric (e.g., 169 newsrooms with 2021/2022 data; 85 with long-term baselines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative organizational development (DEI, practices, community representation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include qualitative assessment elements around diversity, equity and inclusion, sophisticated organizational practices, and representation from served communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use interviews and qualitative data to assess culture shifts, organizational practices, leadership development, and representativeness; treat these as essential complements to numeric sustainability measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing and operational capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate newsroom staffing levels and operational capacity (e.g., full-time staff counts, human capacity to implement changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report average and median staff size and ranges, and consider capacity constraints (lack of human capacity limits ability to implement Table Stakes processes or sustain changes). Use staffing data to contextualize ability to execute revenue/audience strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention-specific effectiveness (audience growth, revenue generation, culture shift)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the relative strengths of different grantee interventions with respect to audience growth, revenue generation, and organizational culture change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare program outcomes (e.g., AJP shows large revenue increases and business-team support; NRH shows DAMU increases for some startups; BloomLab shows revenue growth but DAMU decline). Identify which intervention types (founding investments, hub services, targeted programs) produce which kinds of impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology infrastructure and maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate technology solutions that integrate audience and revenue systems and the newsroom’s ability to maintain those systems over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess technical capacity, the scope of tech changes (e.g., SPS reinvents crucial technology elements), and post-implementation maintenance challenges. Consider whether tech enables revenue generation (donation flows, membership platforms) and whether organizations can sustain upkeep.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mode of support: targeted/customized support vs. training
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate impacts of high-touch, customized support (e.g., coaching, on-site consulting) versus cohort-based training and programming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that customized, expensive support often yields quicker, clearer sustainability gains (examples: AJP success partners, BloomLab consulting), while training (INN, LION, Table Stakes) builds capacity more diffusely and its direct link to sustainability can be harder to observe in short term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer/cohort learning and trust-based relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess benefits from cohort participation and trust-based peer relationships across newsrooms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure the value of peer learning in building capacity, sharing practices across ownership silos, and fostering long-term use of shared approaches; include evidence of continued peer-driven adoption post-program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of performance frameworks and KPIs (Table Stakes principles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate adoption of performance-driven change frameworks such as Table Stakes: design-do, SMART goals, cross-departmental projects, and use of KPIs to determine success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether newsrooms set measurable goals, implement projects, and use KPIs; track long-term retention of these practices and their spread beyond program participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline heterogeneity and interpretation of percent changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Take into account baseline size and heterogeneity when interpreting percent changes in revenue and audience (large baseline organizations can skew averages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both averages and medians, examine top/bottom percentiles (e.g., top 50% saw large average declines while lower 50% saw increases), and avoid over-interpreting mean changes without distributional context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time horizon for evaluation (short-term vs long-term effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate interventions over appropriate time horizons — both immediate (1 year) and multi-year (2–3 years) impacts — recognizing early-stage newsrooms may show rapid early growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect comparable pre/post data at multiple timepoints; interpret short-term gains differently for startups versus established large-audience outlets; track sustainability beyond initial growth spurts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data completeness, representativeness and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for variable data completeness across newsrooms and limitations in data granularity or availability (e.g., SEC-regulated companies unable to provide financial data; inability to separate charitable revenue sources).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document n for each table/metric, note exclusions and data-quality issues, and interpret aggregate findings cautiously. Where breakdowns are unavailable, flag uncertainty (e.g., inability to parse foundation vs individual charitable revenue).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on philanthropic funding and sustainability risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor the extent to which revenue increases are driven by philanthropic/charitable funding and assess the sustainability risk of that reliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report charitable revenue trends (e.g., charitable revenue increased an average of 33.6% from 2021 to 2022) and discuss whether philanthropic support is likely to persist; treat heavy reliance on philanthropy as a potential long-term sustainability vulnerability.
